title: Newfoundland Oil to Electric Rebate 2026: Up to $22,000
desc: Newfoundland and Labrador homes heated with oil can get up to $22,000 to switch to a heat pump, or up to $9,000 above the income line. Rules, income chart and how to apply.
h1: Newfoundland and Labrador Oil to Electric Rebate: Up to $22,000 for a Heat Pump
lead: If you heat your home with oil in Newfoundland and Labrador, the Oil to Electric Incentive Program can pay a large share of the cost of switching to electric heat. A central heat pump can get up to $22,000 for income-qualified households and up to $9,000 for everyone else. The program is open, has no closing date yet, and pays your installer directly, so you may not need to front the money. Everything here comes from the takeCHARGE program page, read on October 16, 2026.
cards_intro: Your amount depends on three things: what you install, your household income and how many people live in your home. These are the maximums. Your real incentive is based on your installer's quote. If you install two systems, you get one incentive, for the one that costs more.

cards.title: Central heat pump
cards.note: Income-qualified households. Up to $9,000 in the general stream. Needs a sized, automatic backup heat source.

cards.title: Multi-split or several mini-splits
cards.note: Income-qualified households. Up to $6,500 in the general stream. Must heat the whole house.

cards.title: Electric furnace or boiler
cards.note: Income-qualified households. Up to $5,000 in the general stream.

cards.title: Oil heating help this winter
cards.note: Separate provincial Home Heating Supplement for oil buyers with 2025 family income of $150,000 or less. Apply by January 15, 2027.

sections: Are you in the income-qualified stream?

The program uses your adjusted net income. That is line 23600 minus line 43500 on your latest tax assessment, for you and your spouse or partner. Count yourself, a second owner if there is one, and anyone else who lives in the home all year.

People in your homeIncome-qualified if income is
1$37,375 or less
2$73,600 or less
3$104,650 or less
4$131,100 or less
5 or more$136,850 or less

Above those lines you are in the general stream. You can still get up to $9,000. Income-qualified homes that get pre-approved for a central, multi-split or multiple mini-split heat pump also get a one-time $250 cheque from Natural Resources Canada in the mail.

• You own the home and it has an active electricity account.
  • It sits on a permanent foundation, is your main home and is lived in all year. New homes do not qualify.
  • It is on the island grid or Labrador's interconnected grid.
  • You can show a 12-month oil statement from the past two years with at least 500 litres. For propane, 1,000 litres.

A warning from the program: an oil tank put in or registered since January 1, 2025, or records that only just reach 500 litres, will get a closer look and may be turned down. Landlords can switch up to two rental homes through the general stream.
What the heat pump has to do

This program pays for whole-home heating, not a single unit in the living room. The heat pump must be an air-source mini-split, multi-split or central system that Natural Resources Canada lists for your climate zone. Your installer signs a form saying it heats the whole house. The program says fewer than 1 in 100 homes can do that with one mini-split.

A central heat pump must come with backup heat that is the right size, wired in and set to turn on by itself. Baseboard heaters are only allowed as backup. The program also warns that a heat pump with no backup heat may void your home insurance, so call your insurer before you book the job.

The money can also cover an electrical panel upgrade if you need one, and removing the oil tank. Take a photo of the tank's HOST tag and serial number before it goes. You will need them for the application.
Why this matters more this winter

Oil got much more expensive this fall. Canadian Press reported furnace oil in St. John's at $2.16 a litre on October 3, 2026, almost a dollar more than a year before. At that price a 900-litre tank costs about $2,240 to fill with tax. A heat pump will not lower this winter's oil bill if the install happens in spring, but every winter after that you buy electricity instead of oil. Read our article on what to do about oil heating bills in Newfoundland for a plan for this winter and the next.
What about the new federal heat pump rebate?

Ottawa announced a National Heat Pump Rebate on October 8, 2026, with a launch expected in early 2027. It has not said how it will work with provincial programs like this one. The Oil to Electric program is open today and has no closing date set, but takeCHARGE says amounts can change with government budgets. See our federal rebate page for what is confirmed so far.
claim_heading: How to apply, step by step
claim_steps: Find an installer on takeCHARGE's participating installer list. Only those installers count. If you like an installer who is not listed, they can email OiltoElectric@TakeChargeNL.ca to join.
Get a written quote with every cost listed: the model numbers, electrical work, labour and materials.

Gather your oil statement (12 months, at least 500 litres), your electricity account number, your spouse or partner's name and SIN if you have one, and a photo of the oil tank's HOST tag and serial number.
Apply online on the takeCHARGE Oil to Electric page, or print the paper application.
Wait for pre-approval before work starts. Your installer then bills the utility for the approved amount, and you pay only what is above it.
faq: How much is the Newfoundland oil to electric rebate?

Up to $22,000 for a central heat pump if your household is income-qualified, or up to $9,000 if not. Multi-split or several mini-splits get up to $18,000 or $6,500. An electric furnace or boiler gets up to $10,000 or $5,000. The incentive can cover up to 100% of the cost.
Is the Oil to Electric program still open?
Yes. On October 16, 2026 the takeCHARGE page said it is still taking applications and no closing date has been set. It also says changes will be announced in advance and suggests applying soon.
Do I have to pay the installer first?
Not for the approved amount. Incentives are paid to your participating installer, who bills Newfoundland Power or Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro directly. You pay any cost above your incentive.
Can I get the program if I heat with propane?
Yes. You need a 12-month propane statement or receipts from the past two years showing at least 1,000 litres.
Can I also get the Home Heating Supplement?

They are separate programs. The Home Heating Supplement pays $400 to $1,000 to residents who buy at least 250 litres of furnace or stove oil and had 2025 family income of $150,000 or less. Applications close January 15, 2027.
I installed a heat pump in 2024. Is it too late?

Maybe not. The program is retroactive to projects finished after April 1, 2023, but you still need a participating installer and the program's paperwork. Email OiltoElectric@TakeChargeNL.ca to check your case.
